The fact chain does the opposite: it records at the granularity of ProseMirror's smallest change unit, the Step, serialized as stepsJson. A single run keeps only one baseJson, and each subsequent message only appends its own stepsJson. This "one base + incremental steps" structure yields three engineering benefits—storage is roughly O(1) baseline plus linear increments, replay order is naturally deterministic, and diff comparison and precise rollback share the same source of truth. The solution is to split rollback semantics into two types by identity boundary and enforce a design principle: the rollback boundary must equal the diff-comparison boundary. Independent Peer has the clearest ownership and naturally independent undo, at the cost of occupying a collaboration seat and increasing permission and sync complexity; Simulated User has the lowest integration cost but completely destroys trust, as users cannot distinguish their own changes from the AI's; Attached Cursor is smoothest in permissions and UX, but without markers the AI and human undo streams get mixed. The author's trade-off is not a three-way choice but an addition on the middle state: let the Agent share the current user's context and permissions as an attached identity, yet stamp each editing round with its own "proof of identity" (session ID / run round / message batch). In essence, it requires both "not creating a virtual colleague" and "not fully masquerading as the user", sinking the ownership boundary into metadata that downstream mechanisms can consume.
